claim: Sensitive data such as personal data, health data, secrets, keys and card numbers is stripped or tokenized on your own device before anything is sent; the real values stay on your device and the answer is rebuilt there.

evidence.note: Client-side DLP: tokenize/scrub runs in the browser before fetch; token->value map is in-memory, device-only (line 9).
Response is rehydrated on-device, so the model never receives the real values when in tokenize mode.
Single DLP engine imported by the CLIENT (src/scrub.js line 10), so the same detectors run in the browser.

risk: Redaction only runs when DLP is active (src/scrub.js isDlpActive, line 24 = an armed governance policy OR the legacy on/off scrub). For a solo user with no armed policy and scrub off, outbound text is NOT scrubbed, yet the marketing states this unconditionally. Honest claim would be 'when data protection is on'.

claim: Each outbound screen frame is checked on your device and any line with a sensitive value is blacked out before the frame leaves; the AI never sees the real sensitive values.

evidence.note: In-browser OCR (tesseract.js from CDN) recognizes frame text and blacks out lines with sensitive values before send. Honest limits noted in the file header (OCR imperfect).
Frame is redacted only when isDlpActive() is true; otherwise the raw dataUrl is sent unmodified (line 29, 2964).

risk: Two caveats vs the unconditional claim: (1) redaction is gated by isDlpActive() - with DLP off, the raw screenshot (sensitive pixels included) is sent; (2) OCR-based blackout is a best-effort backstop, not a guarantee, on downscaled frames (acknowledged in frame_scrub.js but not on the marketing pages).

claim: Stored keys, secrets and report artifacts, including milestone screenshots, are encrypted at rest with AES-256-GCM.

evidence.note: Secrets encrypted on disk with AES-256-GCM; master key from WORK_ENC_KEY or generated .enc.key (0600).
Report screenshot bytes encrypted with the same AES-256-GCM key; writeShot encrypts (line 3640); migration encrypts pre-existing shots (line 159).
Stored report artifacts encrypted at rest with the same key.

risk: Fully backed. Note: the in-memory DB keeps plaintext; at-rest only. A marked-encrypted value that cannot be decrypted throws rather than blanking (no silent failure).

claim: Traffic between devices and the service is protected with TLS (encryption in transit).

evidence.note: No TLS enforcement found in application code (no HTTPS redirect / HSTS in index.js). TLS termination is assumed at the hosting/proxy layer.

risk: TLS is an infrastructure/deployment property, not enforced in the app. Correct in practice behind a TLS proxy, but the app does not itself redirect HTTP->HTTPS or set HSTS, so the claim is deployment-dependent.

claim: WorkCoPilot is read-only by design: it never clicks, types, submits, or changes a system of record on your behalf.
page: WorkSecurity / WorkFaq / WorkTerms / WorkPrivacy / WorkDPA / WorkDisclaimer / WorkMarketing

evidence.note: The server returns guidance text/steps; there is no action-execution endpoint that clicks/types/submits in the user's systems.
Work routes are read/guide/report/metering only; no automation/dispatch route exists.

risk: Backed by architecture (absence of any action-execution path). Cannot be mechanically 'proven' from a single symbol, but no code was found that performs actions in a user system.

claim: Every command, snippet, script and fix is written the secure way and checked for common risks such as injection, hard-coded secrets, over-broad access and known-vulnerable libraries before it reaches you.

evidence.note: Deterministic scanner for dangerous commands + vulnerable dependency versions; HONEST when the vuln lookup cannot run (checkedDeps=false).
Wired into plan (1548), answer-when-code (1772) and another code path (2497); appends user-facing security flags to the session.
Model is instructed to self-review for injection/hardcoded secrets as the primary layer.

risk: Backed, with honest framing on WorkDisclaimer ('a backstop, not a promise'). Nuance: the deterministic gate fires only when the output is classified as code (out.kind/format === 'code'); secure commands embedded in prose answers rely on the prompt layer only.

claim: Multi-factor authentication / step-up protection on sensitive settings (implied by enterprise/security posture).

evidence.note: Dependency-free TOTP; mandatory enrollment on first login per product design.
OTP step-up gate on AI-config endpoints.
Step-up also guards SMTP settings.

risk: Step-up MFA guards only AI-config and SMTP. Other sensitive superadmin mutations (billing secret keys, SSO client secrets, pricing, retention, affiliate payouts, user disable, report-signing key) are NOT step-up gated - inconsistent coverage for an enterprise security posture.

claim: SSO, SAML and invite-only provisioning / SSO / SAML and team provisioning (Enterprise).

evidence.note: Only OIDC single sign-on is implemented (Authorization Code + PKCE). No SAML/assertion handling exists in the module.

risk: The 'SAML' claim is UNBACKED: only OIDC is implemented. Enterprises treat SAML as a distinct protocol requirement; advertising SAML without an implementation is an honesty/sales risk. Invite-only provisioning and OIDC SSO are backed.

claim: Checkout is handled by Stripe, and we never see or store your card number.
page: WorkFaq / WorkPricing / WorkRefund / WorkPrivacy / WorkDPA / AffiliatePage

evidence.note: Payment is via Stripe Checkout/Connect; the app never receives raw PANs. Stored billing config holds Stripe keys only, never card data.

risk: Backed - Stripe-hosted checkout; no card handling in app code.

claim: Learnings are generalized and de-identified: no personal data, secrets, screen images or document content is kept in them.

evidence.note: Stored fact is a short (<=400 char) model-generated generalized string; no screen images or document blobs are stored in the KB.
Backstop strips API-key/token formats, PEM keys, emails, and key=value secret pairs before storing.

risk: Code backstop only strips secrets and emails. It does NOT strip names, phone numbers, SSNs, card numbers, IPs, or account IDs; the 'no personal data' guarantee relies on the model generalizing the fact. Strong claim is only partially code-enforced.

claim: The specific model / vendor in use is never shown to end users; we do not publish vendor or model names.

evidence.symbol: error codes AI-NO-MODEL etc. (model logged only)
evidence.note: User-facing AI errors use opaque refs; model/provider are logged, not surfaced.
Comment + code keep provider/model out of user-facing messages.

risk: Backed by design. Residual: provider catalog (ai.js chatModels lists) is internal; verify no /me or provider-status endpoint leaks the active model string to non-admin users.

claim: Whatever is on your screen or typed into a task is treated as information about the work, never as new instructions; attempts to make it break its own rules are declined and recorded for your administrator.

evidence.note: Detector for prompt-injection/jailbreak/extraction/cross-tenant in user free text; high->refuse, records to abuseCount + superadmin incidents.
Abuse attempts recorded for the administrator.

risk: Backed. The 'treated as information, never instructions' separation is a prompt-architecture property plus the guard; enforcement strength depends on prompt discipline.

claim: Guides work across 156 professional fields in 10 families.

evidence.note: FIELD_TOTAL is derived (sum of items across 10 families); 156 is computed from the roster, not a hardcoded marketing number.
Guidance is grounded per-discipline; memory notes 51 discipline anchors (method coverage is narrower than the 156 advertised fields).

risk: The '156 fields' count is an accurate sum of the roster, but methodology anchors cover ~51 disciplines; fields beyond an anchor fall back to generic guidance. The count claim is honest; the implied depth ('reads like an expert in that field wrote them') is uneven across all 156.

claim: WorkCoPilot plans are Basic $99, Advanced $299 and Premium $399 per month (Lite $69).

evidence.note: Superadmin-editable; marketing fetches /api/work/pricing so the displayed number propagates.
The ACTUAL subscription charge is the Stripe Price ID (priceBasic etc., store.js line 216), a separate config from the displayed pricing.plans.

risk: Display vs charge split: the price SHOWN (pricing.plans, editable) and the price CHARGED (Stripe Price ID) are two independent sources of truth. Changing the displayed price does not change what Stripe charges, so a superadmin can set a displayed price that does not match checkout. Cross-page fallback mismatch also exists: WorkPricing.jsx offline fallback is 199/399/499 vs WorkFaq 99/299/399.

claim: Daily live guidance: 1h Lite / 2h Basic / 4h Advanced / 6h Premium, spent anytime, billed per minute used.

evidence.note: Reads pricing.dailyHours live (superadmin-editable); getWorkUsage derives remaining/exhausted from it (line 2237).
Default 1/2/4/6; change in Admin>Pricing reflects immediately for every user.

risk: Backed and propagating (the recently-fixed path). Fallback constant WORK_TIER_SECONDS (line 2174) still exists but is only used when pricing is unset.

claim: Tasks per day: up to 4 Basic / 8 Advanced / 12 Premium / Unlimited Enterprise.

evidence.note: Reads pricing.tasks live; company/corporate = unlimited. Enforced server-side as a daily hard gate.

risk: Backed and superadmin-editable (pricing.tasks).

claim: Per-task re-plan budget (a re-plan re-adapts the plan with new info and never changes the original request).

evidence.note: Default 5/10/10/10, superadmin-editable; corporate unlimited.

risk: Backed and editable.

claim: Top up extra guided hours at $10 per hour on any plan; purchased time never expires.

evidence.note: Overage priced dynamically from pricing.hour[tier] (superadmin-editable) via Stripe price_data - propagates correctly.
Purchased seconds are a persistent balance (no expiry).

risk: The $10/hr is from pricing.hour (default lite 25/basic 20/advanced 15/premium 10). WorkPricing/WorkFaq state a flat '$10/hour, every plan', but the per-tier default hour rate is NOT flat ($25/$20/$15/$10). The flat $10 copy matches only the premium tier's default.

claim: Premium adds generated visuals on demand; image packs start from <price> each (min <N>). Premium free allowance is 5/day.

evidence.note: Per-image price and bulk minimum are superadmin-editable and shown live.
The daily FREE generation allowance { lite:0, basic:0, advanced:0, premium:5 } is HARDCODED - not superadmin-editable.
Server enforces premium-only image generation (hardcoded string compare, not via a tier-feature registry).

risk: Image PRICE/min propagate, but the '5/day' free allowance and the premium-only gate are hardcoded constants - an operator cannot change them without a code change (same class as the recently-fixed daily-hours bug).

claim: Roadmaps (Basic+), own-document grounding (Advanced+), generated visuals/diagrams (Premium).

evidence.note: Feature gates { roadmaps, diagrams, documents } are HARDCODED per tier; exposed to the client as caps (line 453).
Document upload gate is a SECOND hardcoded set ['advanced','premium'] rather than reading store.tierAllows - a parallel source of truth.
The guidance endpoint returns the roadmap array to ALL tiers; no server-side tierAllows('roadmaps') check. Lite/Basic gating is client-side only (via caps).

risk: (1) TIER_FEATURES is hardcoded and not superadmin-editable. (2) Document gate duplicates the truth in work-docs.js. (3) Roadmap/diagram tier gate is NOT enforced server-side (only advertised in caps), so a direct API call from a Lite/Basic account can receive roadmap data it did not pay for. Documents and images ARE server-enforced; roadmaps/diagrams are not - inconsistent enforcement.

claim: By default sessions are kept until you or your admin delete them; an automatic retention window can be configured so sessions older than N days are purged on a schedule.

evidence.note: Two-tier retention (platform for solo, company admin for members); 0 = keep forever.
Purges sessions past the effective window; removes shots + audit.
Sweep wired; also runs immediately when retention is set (lines 1118, 1265). Propagates.

risk: Backed and propagating. Note WorkPrivacy glance text ('There is no automatic retention timer yet') contradicts the configurable-window copy elsewhere on the same site - stale sentence.

claim: If a payment fails, we may limit access to paid features until it is resolved.

evidence.note: Returns true only for trialing/active/comp (and covered company members); past_due/canceled are excluded.
Enforced on the guidance path (lines 204, 214). past_due/canceled -> 402.
Failed renewal flips status so guiding blocks automatically.

risk: Backed. Note: admin/superadmin bypass both subscription and time gates (index.js line 189) for operator testing.

claim: Company admins can end a member's access; a disabled account is blocked from all service.

evidence.note: Disabled user or disabled company -> 403 immediately, before billing branch; session epoch bump signs them out everywhere.

risk: Backed and propagates immediately.

claim: You earn 30% of each referral's first payment, paid automatically through Stripe; renewals and later purchases do not earn commission.

evidence.note: Commission = amount*ratePct% on the FIRST payment only (deduped by refUserId, line 3369).
Payout transfers the earned balance to the affiliate's connected Stripe account, respecting minPayoutUsd.
30% is the fallback; the live rate is store.getAffiliateConfig().defaultRatePct (superadmin-editable).

risk: First-payment-only and Stripe payout are backed and the rate is editable.

claim: Commission is voided if the payment is refunded or reversed.

evidence.note: Refund webhook records a 'refund' transaction in the ledger but does NOT touch the affiliate referral.
A referral is only set to 'void' when the AFFILIATE was suspended at conversion time - never on a refund/chargeback of the referred payment.

risk: UNBACKED: no code voids or reverses an affiliate commission when the referred user's first payment is refunded or charged back. A refunded referral can still be paid out. This is both a claims honesty risk and a revenue-leak business bug.

claim: Per-company presets for frameworks such as GDPR, HIPAA, PCI DSS, SOC 2 and ISO 27001 are one click to arm and lock.

evidence.note: 8 armable DLP presets exist (GDPR, HIPAA, PCI, CCPA, EU, US-CA, India DPDP, UK).
18 frameworks for report/evidence mapping (SOC2, ISO 27001, NIST, etc.) - these are evidence mappings, not arm-able redaction presets.

risk: SOC 2 and ISO 27001 are named as 'one click to arm' presets but have NO arm-able redaction preset in compliance-presets.js (they are evidence/control frameworks only). 'such as' softens it, but naming them specifically as presets overstates what arms. GDPR/HIPAA/PCI presets are fully backed.

claim: WorkCoPilot is compliance-ready across the frameworks you report to; it gives controls and audit evidence, and we do not claim a certification.
page: WorkSecurity / WorkFaq / WorkTerms / WorkPrivacy / WorkDPA / WorkDisclaimer

evidence.note: 18 frameworks mapped to on-device redaction + audit log + read-only + role-based policy as supporting evidence.
'a disclosure of what the product does today, not a compliance claim'; 'we do not claim a certification'.

risk: Honestly framed (explicit non-certification language). The underlying controls (redaction, audit log, read-only, role policy) exist.

claim: A per-session audit log records what was transmitted, so you can see exactly what left your device; company admins can review their members' sessions.

evidence.note: Session events (flags, sends) recorded per session; retained with the report and encrypted at rest.
Company admins can review their own members' sessions/reports.

risk: Backed.

claim: Upload your own documents; they are read on your computer and the file never leaves your device.

evidence.note: Only governed/extracted text is stored on disk; the raw file is not kept as source material.

evidence.symbol: 'Text is extracted on our server, scrubbed'
evidence.note: For the BROWSER upload path, document text is extracted ON THE SERVER, not on-device.

risk: 'Read on your computer, the file never leaves' is true for the DESKTOP app only. On the browser path the file is uploaded and text is extracted server-side. WorkFaq/WorkPrivacy correctly qualify '(desktop app)', but WorkCapabilities states 'read on your computer, the file never leaving' without the desktop qualifier - overbroad for browser users.

claim: Show it a diagram/architecture/design: it finds the issues and hands you a ready-to-use prompt to generate the corrected version in your own tools.

evidence.symbol: promptIssues deliverable (paste into your own LLM/diagram tool)
evidence.note: Produces a self-contained prompt for the user's own tool rather than generating the artifact - matches the stated no-generation design.

risk: Backed (consistent with the product's no-document-generation policy).

claim: +70% faster to done, -50% outsourcing spend, 100% read-only, weeks -> days to market.

evidence.note: No benchmark/telemetry source backs the +70% / -50% / weeks->days figures. '100% read-only' maps to the read-only architecture.

risk: The percentage ROI figures are marketing illustrations with no measured source in code or data; '100% read-only' is backed. If presented as measured outcomes they are an unsubstantiated-performance-claim risk (the Exec dashboard labels similar numbers 'hypothetical', which these are not).

claim: Annual billing saves 20% (a free month for referred users on annual).

evidence.note: The 20% annual math is a client-side literal in the marketing page.
Actual annual charge is a separate Stripe annual Price ID; the 20% is display math only.

risk: The displayed 20% discount is computed client-side and is independent of the actual annual Stripe Price. If the annual Stripe Price is not set to exactly 80% x 12, the shown saving will not match the charge (same display-vs-charge split as monthly).

claim: The plan always comes from the strongest option actually available; if anything changed mid-task the log says so (honest by design, nothing silently rerouted).

evidence.note: Retired-model self-heal against live catalog; failover records every switch as an incident (per ai_failover test).
Opaque error refs; a missing model surfaces a reason rather than silently swapping provider.

risk: Backed by the failover/incident design (SUPREME RULE III). 'Strongest AI' is a subjective label; the code picks a dependable current model, not a measured 'strongest'.

claim: For Enterprise/sales we reply within one business day; Enterprise gets a priority SLA.

evidence.note: No code enforces or measures a one-business-day response or a priority SLA; support is email-based.

risk: Response-time/SLA promises are operational commitments with no system backing (no ticket-SLA timer). Acceptable as a human commitment, but there is no mechanism ensuring it.
